Home • Data • State Taxes • State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026 See previous versions of this post State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026 February 17, 2026 February 19, 2026 9 min read By: Janelle Fritts , Katherine Loughead Download 2026 Data Table of Contents Individual income taxes are a major source of state government revenue, accounting for 33 percent of state tax collections in fiscal year 2024, the latest year for which data are available.

(Adjusted for inflation, these amounts have increased to $16,100 and $32,200, respectively, for tax year 2026.

Specifically, in states that conform to the federal standard deduction generally but have not yet updated their conformity dates to a post-OBBBA version of the IRC, those states now conform to the pre-TCJA federal standard deduction amount, which, adjusted for inflation, is $8,350 for single filers and $16,700 for joint filers for tax year 2026.

Though barely 100 years old, individual income taxes are the largest source rates, brackets, standard deductions, and personal exemptions for both single and joint filers as of February 11, 2026.

Following the tables, we document notable individual income tax changes implemented in 2026.

Inflation-adjusted bracket widths for 2026 were not available as of publication, so table reflects 2025 inflation-adjusted bracket widths.

The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act set the personal exemption to $0 until 2026 but did not eliminate it, and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act permanently set the personal exemption to $0 but did not eliminate it.

(n) Standard deduction and/or personal exemption adjusted annually for inflation, but the 2026 inflation adjustment was not available at time of publication, so table reflects actual 2025 amount(s).
